title: Multistep parallel synthesis in a 96-vial reaction block with block-level workup and LC-MS yields
summary: A three-step modular synthesis run in a 96-vial stirred reaction block (Para-dox style), where building block stocks are dosed by volume, steps run overnight to two days, and crude mixtures are worked up in-block and quantified by LC-MS against an internal standard. Gives realistic dosing volumes and step durations for a block-based cascade.

steps.text: Prepare 0.25 M stock solutions of 8 carbonyl building blocks and the sulfinamide partner; dose about 80 uL of each per vial plus about 40 mg solid base.
Stir the first reaction at room temperature for 14 h.
Add toluene (about 400 uL), stir 5 min at 1000 rpm, centrifuge and extract to get crude intermediate.
Add the bifunctional reagent, Ni catalyst and Zn powder, stir 48 h at room temperature.
Add photocatalyst and silyl triflate solutions (about 50 uL each) and irradiate with blue light for 20 h.
Quench with ammonia in acetonitrile (about 600 uL per vial), stir 10 min, then concentrate, exchange solvent and filter.
Take aliquots of the crude mixtures and run LC-MS with an internal standard (1,3,5-trimethoxybenzene) to get yields by peak-area ratio.

materials: Aldehyde/ketone stocks, sulfinamide, Cs2CO3, Ni catalyst, Zn nanopowder, TMSOTf, pyrylium photocatalyst
safety: Zn nanopowder, TMSOTf and ammonia need ventilated handling; blue-light reactor shielding.
notes: This is a SLAP-reagent cascade, not Suzuki; used as a block-format multistep analogue. Equipment mapping is ours.
